bullets.text: I’m seeing that **phishing** is increasingly targeting individuals rather than just systems, with 95% of successful attacks involving human error, highlighting the need for vigilance.
I noticed that **Making Tax Digital (MTD)** for Income Tax is set to revolutionise personal tax, requiring digital accounting for sole traders and landlords starting April 2026.
I’m learning that the MTD initiative will phase out traditional Self Assessment tax returns for landlords, starting with those earning over £50,000 in April 2026.
I see that sole traders will also transition to MTD for Income Tax, with new digital requirements beginning for those earning over £50,000 in April 2026.
I’m discovering that MTD for Income Tax will automate many accounting tasks, allowing businesses to focus more on growth rather than admin.
I’m aware that effective financial record keeping is crucial for landlords, especially with the potential tax implications of not maintaining proper records.
I’m seeing that accountants will play a vital role in guiding clients through the MTD for Income Tax transition, which begins in April 2026 for many.
I’ve noted that landlords will need to adapt to new quarterly reporting requirements under MTD for Income Tax, moving away from annual Self Assessment returns.
I’m learning that MTD for Income Tax is a significant shift in tax management, requiring digital record keeping and regular submissions to HMRC.
I’m noticing that MTD for Income Tax will impact millions of sole traders and landlords, marking one of the biggest changes in tax for a generation.
